Strait of Hormuz Status: October 4, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  217 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
4 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.25 -0.11 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 The Times of Israel reports US Defense Secretary Hegseth called the American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz 'ironclad'; the claim has not been independently confirmed.

02 CGTN and multiple regional outlets report Iran's IRGC claims to have struck seven tankers in the Strait of Hormuz over five days; no major wire in this feed carries this.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 1 vessel transiting on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with IMF PortWatch recording just 1 vessel transiting on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The most significant diplomatic development in this window is a report from The Times of Israel that US Defense Secretary Hegseth described the American blockade as 'ironclad'; the claim has not been independently confirmed. On the operational side, CGTN reports the IRGC claims to have struck seven tankers it describes as 'violating' the strait over five days; no major wire in this feed carries the claim. Iraq's state tanker firm is reported by Investing.com to be continuing to move crude through the strait, though no major wire in this feed carries that item. Brent crude stood at $102.25 as of 05:49 UTC, down 0.11% in the last session before the close; futures are shut and that figure has not moved since. The wider context remains unchanged: Iran's seven-day reopening proposal was publicly rejected by President Trump on September 26, and Iran has said it will not soften its terms, while Iran says it received a US response to its plan on September 30 and is reviewing it. As of 05:50 UTC, 139 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
